I am 55 years old and have farmed in Quzhou County for more than 30 years. My family has 10 mu of flat, irrigated land on the North China Plain. Last October I sowed winter wheat, and now that the weather has warmed up the wheat is greening and needs topdressing fertilizer. I will stick with what I know: winter wheat followed by summer maize on all 10 mu. I am not growing cotton this year. The cotton price is uncertain, and spraying pesticides sixteen times a season is too hard on my back and too much labor for just me and my wife. Wheat and maize are easier—only about four pesticide applications each—and I can hire a combine harvester for both. For the wheat, I will apply spring topdressing fertilizer and irrigate three times in total, including the winter irrigation I already gave it and two more in spring. I expect about 1,100 jin per mu, which is 550 kg. After harvesting the wheat in early June, I will plant hybrid maize using no-tillage seeding directly into the wheat stubble. This saves fuel and time, and the seed dealer in town sells reliable hybrid varieties. I will side-dress nitrogen when the maize is knee-high, irrigate twice during the summer, spray for weeds and borers four times, and harvest in late September. I expect about 1,150 jin per mu, or 575 kg. This double-cropping system feeds my family and gives me grain to sell, and it is the right amount of work for us.
